nave.definition: The long central space of a church, running from the entrance toward the altar. It is where the congregation stands.

pointed-arch.definition: An arch of two curves meeting at a point. It sends its load down more steeply than a round arch, so builders could go taller and make arches of different widths reach the same height.

rib-vault.definition: A stone ceiling built on a frame of crossing arched ribs. The ribs gather the weight onto a few points, so the panels between them can be thinner and lighter.

flying-buttress.definition: An arched prop outside the building. It carries the outward push of the high vault over the side aisles to a heavy outer pier, so the upper walls no longer need to be thick.

triforium.definition: A narrow arcaded band in the wall, above the main arches and below the upper windows.

clerestory.definition: The upper level of the nave wall, filled with windows that light the middle of the church.

rose-window.definition: A large circular window divided by stone tracery into radiating sections, often filled with stained glass.

twin-spires.definition: A pair of towers with spires framing the main west entrance. It is a common way to give a Gothic façade height and symmetry.

buildings.name: Notre-Dame de Chartres
buildings.tagline: Built in about 26 years, and its glass mostly survived.

construction.quote: it was mostly constructed between 1194 and 1220

attested_features.quote: The building's exterior is dominated by heavy flying buttresses which allowed the architects to increase the window size significantly
the majority of the original stained glass windows survive intact

scenes.title: A site older than its stones
scenes.caption: At least five cathedrals have stood on this spot since the diocese was founded. The building you see is the latest layer.
scenes.quote: It stands on the site of at least five cathedrals that have occupied the site since the Diocese of Chartres was formed as an episcopal see in the 4th century.

scenes.title: Gothic on Romanesque foundations
scenes.caption: The Gothic church rises from earlier Romanesque basements. One style is literally built on top of the other.
scenes.quote: It was built above earlier Romanesque basements

scenes.title: A cathedral in a generation
scenes.caption: Most of the cathedral went up in about 26 years. That speed is one reason it has such a consistent style.
scenes.quote: it was mostly constructed between 1194 and 1220

scenes.title: Props outside, light inside
scenes.caption: Heavy flying buttresses carry the vault's push outside the walls. That freed the walls to hold much bigger windows.
scenes.quote: The building's exterior is dominated by heavy flying buttresses which allowed the architects to increase the window size significantly

scenes.title: The original glass
scenes.caption: Most of the original stained glass windows survive intact, which is rare for a building this old.
scenes.quote: the majority of the original stained glass windows survive intact

scenes.title: A destination for travellers
scenes.caption: People have travelled here for at least 850 years, first as pilgrims, and now as visitors too.
scenes.quote: Since at least the 12th century the cathedral has been an important destination for travellers.

buildings.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
buildings.tagline: Where Gothic's signature parts were pioneered, and rebuilt more than once.

construction.quote: The construction of the cathedral began in 1163 under Bishop Maurice de Sully and was largely completed by 1260

attested_features.quote: its pioneering use of the rib vault and flying buttress
its pioneering use of the rib vault and flying buttress
its enormous and colourful rose windows

scenes.title: A bishop starts building
scenes.caption: Construction began under Bishop Maurice de Sully and was largely finished about a century later.
scenes.quote: The construction of the cathedral began in 1163 under Bishop Maurice de Sully and was largely completed by 1260

scenes.title: Leaving Romanesque behind
scenes.caption: Rib vaults and flying buttresses set it apart from the earlier Romanesque style, along with its huge rose windows.
scenes.quote: its pioneering use of the rib vault and flying buttress

scenes.title: Revolution
scenes.caption: During the French Revolution, much of its religious imagery was damaged or destroyed.
scenes.quote: In the 1790s, during the French Revolution, Notre-Dame suffered extensive desecration

scenes.title: A novel saves a building
scenes.caption: Victor Hugo's novel revived public interest, which led to a restoration led by Viollet-le-Duc.
scenes.quote: The 1831 publication of Victor Hugo's novel Notre-Dame de Paris (English title: The Hunchback of Notre-Dame) inspired interest which led to restoration between 1844 and 1864, supervised by Eugène Viollet-le-Duc.

scenes.title: Fire, then reopening
scenes.caption: A fire in April 2019 caused serious damage. After extensive repairs, the cathedral reopened in December 2024.
scenes.quote: A fire in April 2019 caused serious damage, closing the cathedral for extensive and costly repairs; it reopened in December 2024.

buildings.name: Cologne Cathedral
buildings.tagline: A medieval plan that took more than 600 years to finish.

construction.quote: Construction of Cologne Cathedral began in 1248

attested_features.quote: The towers for its two huge spires give the cathedral the largest façade of any church in the world.

scenes.title: A home for the Three Kings
scenes.caption: The builders planned a grand structure to hold the reliquary of the Three Kings.
scenes.quote: Cologne's medieval builders had planned a grand structure to house the reliquary of the Three Kings

scenes.title: Work stops
scenes.caption: Construction halted in the years around 1560 and stayed unfinished for centuries.
scenes.quote: Construction of Cologne Cathedral began in 1248, but was halted in the years around 1560.

scenes.title: A revival picks it up again
scenes.caption: Efforts to finish it began around 1814, but proper funding only came in the 1840s.
scenes.quote: Attempts to complete construction began around 1814, but the project was not properly funded until the 1840s.

scenes.title: Finished to the medieval plan
scenes.caption: It was completed in 1880, following the original medieval design.
scenes.quote: The edifice was completed to its original medieval plan in 1880.

scenes.title: 157 metres of Gothic
scenes.caption: It is the tallest twin-spired church in the world.
scenes.quote: At 157 m (515 ft), the cathedral is the tallest twin-spired church in the world

buildings.name: Notre-Dame d'Amiens
buildings.tagline: Built to reach for the heavens and let in light.

construction.quote: The cathedral was built almost entirely between 1220 and c. 1270

attested_features.quote: The Rayonnant appeared in the triforium and clerestory, which were begun in 1236
The Rayonnant appeared in the triforium and clerestory, which were begun in 1236

scenes.title: Fifty years, one style
scenes.caption: Built in a short span for a Gothic cathedral, which gives it an unusually unified style.
scenes.quote: The cathedral was built almost entirely between 1220 and c. 1270, a remarkably short period of time for a Gothic cathedral, giving it an unusual unity of style.

scenes.title: Rayonnant arrives
scenes.caption: The new Rayonnant style appears in the triforium and clerestory, the upper levels of the wall.
scenes.quote: The Rayonnant appeared in the triforium and clerestory, which were begun in 1236

scenes.title: Height and light
scenes.caption: The builders pushed the inside as large as they could, to reach upward and bring in more light.
scenes.quote: Its builders were trying to maximize the internal dimensions in order to reach for the heavens and bring in more light.

scenes.title: Twice Notre-Dame
scenes.caption: It is the largest cathedral by volume in France, more than double Notre-Dame de Paris.
scenes.quote: Amiens Cathedral is the largest by volume in France, 200,000 cubic metres (260,000 cu yd), more than double the volume of Notre Dame of Paris.

scenes.title: Stone that tells stories
scenes.caption: It is known for the quality and quantity of its early 13th-century Gothic sculpture.
scenes.quote: Amiens Cathedral is renowned for the quality and quantity of early 13th-century Gothic sculpture in the main west façade
